text:
### Observed differences

- Two groups of activities exchanged their place in the sequence. In the earlier window, A20, A22 and A23 (present in every trace) sat at a median event position of about 0.39, followed by A25 (about 0.44) and A29 (about 0.65), with the optional group A19, A21 and A24 (present in roughly 30–38 of 100 traces) last at about 0.68–0.70. In the later window, A19, A21 and A24 sit early at about 0.34–0.36, A25 follows at about 0.38 and A29 at about 0.59, while A20, A22 and A23 moved back to about 0.64–0.66. Participation shifted slightly: A19 now appears in about 44 of 100 traces (about 31 before), A21 in about 29 (about 38 before). [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009]

- The pairwise orders reversed almost completely. A20 came before A25 in about 98 of 100 traces before and in none after, while A25 now precedes A20 in all traces; A22 and A23 show the same near-total flips against A25 and A29 (for example, A22 preceded A29 in every earlier trace, and A29 now precedes A22 in about 98 of 100). [REL017, REL018, REL024, REL025, REL027, REL028]

- Orders between the optional group and the rest flipped as well. Where both occurred, A19 preceded A20, A22, A23 or A25 in essentially no earlier trace but in essentially all such later traces (about 44 in 100 traces overall, up from about 31 with the opposite order); A20 preceded A21 in about 37 of 100 traces before, whereas A21 now precedes A20 in about 29 of 100; comparable reversals hold for A20/A22/A23 against A24 and for A21/A24 against A25/A29. [REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL026, REL029, REL030]

- Direct hand-offs changed accordingly. Of A19's observed outgoing transitions, about 97 in 100 went to A30 before and about 97 in 100 go to A25 after; A21 (about 99 in 100 to A30 before, all to A25 after) and A24 (about 97 to A30 before, about 95 to A25 after) show the same switch. Conversely, A20, A22 and A23 lost A25 as a successor (about 30–39 of their observed outgoing transitions before, about 0–0.5 in 100 after) and gained A30 (about 32–34 in 100 after), and A29's outgoing transitions moved from A21, A19 and A24 to A20, A22 and A23. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008]

- A02 became a regular early step: it appears in about 34 of 100 later traces versus about 8 of 100 earlier ones, at a median position of about 0.33 versus 0.53. A40 precedes A02 in about 31 of 100 later traces (about 5 of 100 before), A02 precedes A20, A22, A23, A25, A29 and A30 in roughly 32–33 of 100 traces (about 3–5 of 100 before), and its observed outgoing transitions now go mainly to A19 (about 37 in 100), A24 (about 27) and A21 (about 24), where before they were spread over A15, A44, A23 and several minor targets. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR009, REL002, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009]

- A41 is repeated more often: mean occurrences per trace rose from about 1.5 to about 1.8 and recurrence support from about 0.33 to 0.40, while it remains present in every trace in both windows. [OCC002]

- A43's routing stayed essentially stable (about 93 of 100 observed outgoing transitions to A44 before, about 98 after), so the reorganisation did not touch every activity. [DIR010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the two activity groups exchanged their order in the later window: the group A19, A21 and A24, which previously ran after A20, A22 and A23 with A25 and A29 in between, now runs before them, and the hand-offs flipped — A19, A21 and A24 now lead to A25 instead of A30, while A20, A22 and A23 lead to A30 instead of A25. The order change is shown directly by the relation data, where the earlier fixed orders (for example A20 before A25 in about 98 of 100 traces) are replaced by the opposite fixed orders (A25 before A20 in all traces), and the two groups' positions moved in opposite directions, which rules out an apparent shift caused by uniformly longer or shorter traces. The direction data agrees with the reversal, and the screening result (51 qualifying control-flow items against roughly 0.64 expected without change, about 80 times that expectation) is far beyond what an unchanged process produces. [REL017, REL024, REL025, REL027, REL010, POS002, POS003, POS005, POS006, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007]

The many relation, position and direction items describe one underlying reorganisation, so they are not independent confirmations, and the optional group is observed only in the roughly 29–44 of 100 traces in which its activities occur; about 1–2 in 100 later traces show interleaved or repeated execution, so a small residual of other orders cannot be excluded. One competing explanation remains open: the data establish the new pairwise orders but cannot settle whether the two groups cleanly exchanged places or the whole segment was re-sequenced, since A25 and A29 also drifted a little (median positions about 0.44 to 0.38 and about 0.67 to 0.59); positions are event ranks, not clock times. [REL018, REL025, REL028, POS008, POS009]

Other differences: A02 became much more frequent (about 8 to about 34 of 100 traces) and now sits early in the trace, typically after A40 and before the A19/A21/A24 group, to which most of its outgoing transitions lead; whether this placement belongs to the same reorganisation or is an independent participation change cannot be decided from this evidence. A41 is repeated more often (mean occurrences per trace up from about 1.5 to about 1.8). [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR009, REL002, REL008, REL009, OCC002]
